source_caption:
Peter O’Toole completely anchors the bombastic, sprawling spectacle of *Troy* with a singular, quiet moment of devastating, Shakespearean grief. When King Priam secretly enters the enemy camp to beg Achilles for the mutilated body of his slain son, O’Toole strips away every ounce of his royal pride, delivering an absolute masterclass in raw, agonizing vulnerability. By weeping as he kisses the bloodstained hands of his son’s killer, the legendary actor single-handedly elevates a massive Hollywood blockbuster into a profound classical tragedy. He brilliantly proves that the most breathtaking, powerful sequence in a massive war epic isn’t a sweeping battle at all, but an exhausted, heartbroken father simply pleading for the right to mourn.
⠀
Troy (2004), directed by Wolfgang Petersen, starring Brad Pitt, Eric Bana, Orlando Bloom, Peter O’Toole. When a forbidden royal romance sparks a catastrophic conflict between two ancient superpowers, a massive Greek armada lays siege to the impenetrable city of Troy, drawing legendary warriors into a brutal, devastating war driven by honor, glory, and inescapable fate.

source_details.synopsis: Troy is a 2004 epic historical action film directed by Wolfgang Petersen and written by David Benioff. Produced by units in Malta, Mexico, and Britain's Shepperton Studios, the film features an ensemble cast led by Brad Pitt, Eric Bana, Orlando Bloom, Diane Kruger, Sean Bean, Brian Cox, Brendan Gleeson, Rose Byrne, and Peter O'Toole. It is loosely based on Homer's Iliad in its narration of the entire story of the decade-long Trojan War—condensed into little more than a couple of weeks, rather than just the quarrel between Achilles and Agamemnon in the ninth year.
